stories.title: Atlantic Capital Partners Arranges $10M Sale of Milford Strip Center
stories.excerpt: Atlantic Capital Partners arranged the $10-million sale of Quarry Square, a 56,004-square-foot, stabilized neighborhood strip center in Milford, MA, anchored by local fitness and restaurant operators. The transaction was led by head of capital markets Justin Smith, EVP Chris Peterson, senior associate Danielle Turpin and associate Matt Ericson, representing the sellers, RJ Kelly. Quarry Square is currently 100% leased to 17 retail tenants, providing new ownership with immediate stability. “The asset offers an exceptional combination of durable, long-term cash flow and embedded upside,” said Smith. “The center features a diverse, resilient tenant mix with a proven track record of lease renewals. With several leases nearing expiration, incoming ownership has a clear runway to boost net operating income by bringing below-market rents to fair market value upon rollover.” The 8.6-acre property is situated along East Main Street, the submarket’s primary corridor connecting Milford to I-495 and the broader regional markets of Boston, Worcester and Lowell. The post Atlantic Capital Partners Arranges $10M Sale of Milford Strip Center appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Atlantic Capital arranges $10M sale of 56,004-sf Quarry Square strip center, Milford MA.
100% leased to 17 tenants; several leases near expiration create NOI upside via rent rollover.
Located on East Main Street corridor connecting to I-495, Boston, Worcester, Lowell markets.
stories.summary: Atlantic Capital Partners sold Quarry Square, a fully leased 56,004-sf neighborhood retail center in Milford, MA, for $10 million. The property's 17 tenants (fitness, restaurant operators) provide immediate cash flow, with multiple lease expirations creating runway to increase NOI by bringing below-market rents to fair market value. Positioned on the primary East Main Street corridor with access to I-495 and Boston/Worcester/Lowell metros.
stories.impact: Minimal direct multifamily relevance; this is stabilized retail. However, the deal signals investor appetite for Boston-area suburban corridors with I-95 access—noting Milford's proximity to major metros may indicate healthy regional demand for infill residential in secondary-tier suburbs near employment centers.

stories.title: SoCal Family Office Snaps Up Apartments in Competitive Modesto Submarket
stories.excerpt: The Mogharebi Group (TMG) represented Bay Area-based Tesseract Capital Group in the sale of The Marc at 1600, a 100-unit multifamily community located at 1600 Standiford Ave. in Modesto. The buyer was a private family office from Southern California, which paid $26.6 million. TMG’s team of EVP Otto Ozen, SVP Brian Nakamura and SVP Nazli Santana represented the seller. “This property offered the buyer an exceptional opportunity to establish immediate scale and a meaningful foothold in one of the region’s most competitive submarkets, supported by a loan structure that enhances financial efficiency in today’s high‑rate environment,” said Nakamura. “The buyer intends to maintain seamless operational continuity for residents while optimizing backend systems to drive yield and elevate long‑term asset performance.” The Marc at 1600 benefits from institutional quality and a supply-constrained market, according to TMG. The property was well capitalized and contained an assumable HUD loan of 3.8% loan. The post SoCal Family Office Snaps Up Apartments in Competitive Modesto Submarket appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: SoCal family office acquires The Marc at 1600, 100-unit Modesto apt, $26.6M.
Property includes assumable HUD loan at 3.8%—below-market fixed rate enhances buyer economics.
Modesto supply-constrained market; buyer aims yield optimization and operational efficiency.
stories.summary: A Southern California family office purchased The Marc at 1600, a 100-unit apartment community in Modesto, for $26.6 million. The deal included assumption of a 3.8% HUD loan, providing a significant financing advantage in today's higher-rate environment. TMG noted the property benefits from institutional quality and a supply-constrained submarket, with the buyer planning operational optimization to drive yield and long-term performance.
stories.impact: In Modesto's supply-constrained market, this acquisition signals sustained multifamily investor confidence and highlights the strategic value of assumable below-market debt to justify acquisition prices—a critical funding lever for developers evaluating Modesto's rental demand and feasibility. The 3.8% loan cushion makes value-add repositioning more attractive despite high current borrowing costs.

stories.title: Roche, Genentech Cut Ribbon on Allston Innovation Center
stories.excerpt: Genentech, a member of the Roche Group, held the grand opening of the Roche Genentech Innovation Center Boston in Allston. Roche and Genentech have signed a 10-year lease for the 95,000-square-foot center, which has capacity for up to 500 people and which anchors the first phase of the Enterprise Research Campus (ERC), a nine-acre development by Tishman Speyer and Breakthrough Properties in partnership with the Harvard Allston Land Company. “This investment in Boston is an important part of our commitment to expand our U.S. manufacturing and R&D footprint,” said Dr. Thomas Schinecker, Roche CEO. “By investing in scientific talent, new capabilities and infrastructure, we are strengthening our ability to discover and develop the next generation of medicines for patients.” The center complements established R&D teams in South San Francisco and Basel while connecting Roche and Genentech scientists more closely with researchers, talent and institutions across the Boston scientific and biotech ecosystem. The post Roche, Genentech Cut Ribbon on Allston Innovation Center appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Roche/Genentech opens 95,000-sf Innovation Center, Boston Allston; 10-year lease, 500-person capacity.
Anchors first phase of Enterprise Research Campus (Tishman Speyer, Breakthrough Properties, Harvard).
Signals major biotech R&D expansion, talent influx to Boston scientific ecosystem.
stories.summary: Genentech, a Roche subsidiary, held the grand opening of a 95,000-sf Innovation Center Boston in Allston, under a 10-year lease with capacity for 500 employees. The facility anchors the first phase of the nine-acre Enterprise Research Campus, a mixed-use development by Tishman Speyer and Breakthrough Properties in partnership with Harvard. Roche CEO Thomas Schinecker emphasized this as a commitment to expand U.S. manufacturing and R&D footprint and strengthen ties with Boston's scientific talent pool.
stories.impact: Major employer expansion in Boston Allston directly signals incoming talent and job growth—300+ new biotech/R&D roles will drive residential demand in nearby neighborhoods (Allston, Brighton, Cambridge, Beacon Hill). Developers should evaluate multifamily acquisition, entitlement, and build timing in walkable Allston-Brighton and Cambridge submarkets within 1–2 years to capture rent growth from incoming Roche/Genentech workforce and spillover biotech hiring.

stories.title: Galvanize Real Estate Makes California Debut with Milpitas Industrial Portfolio
stories.excerpt: Galvanize Real Estate (GRE), the real estate platform of Tom Steyer’s climate firm Galvanize, has made its first California acquisition with a deal for the Cadillac Court Industrial Portfolio, a four-building campus in Milpitas. The San Francisco Chronicle reported the purchase price as $94 million. Newmark executive vice chairman and president, Western Region Capital Markets Steve Golubchik, vice chairman Edmund Najera, senior managing director Darren Hollak and director Brendan Raney represented the seller, reported as DRA Advisors. Newmark executive managing director Kevin Hatcher advised on the sale of the property as a local market expert. “The Silicon Valley industrial market is seeing stronger leasing activity, declining vacancy and more demand from advanced manufacturing and AI-driven companies,” said Golubchik. “Cadillac Court offered the opportunity to invest in that momentum in one of the Bay Area’s most tightly held industrial submarkets.” Built between 1991 and 1994, the 300,000-square-foot campus is approximately 95% leased. GRE plans a series of energy-efficiency upgrades. The post Galvanize Real Estate Makes California Debut with Milpitas Industrial Portfolio appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Galvanize Real Estate acquires Cadillac Court Industrial Portfolio, Milpitas, $94M (four-building, 300k sf).
95% leased; strong leasing, declining vacancy driven by advanced manufacturing and AI demand.
Silicon Valley industrial market tightly held; GRE plans energy-efficiency upgrades.
stories.summary: Galvanize Real Estate (Tom Steyer's climate firm) made its California debut with a $94 million purchase of the Cadillac Court Industrial Portfolio, a 300,000-sf, four-building campus in Milpitas built 1991–1994 and 95% leased. The deal capitalized on stronger Silicon Valley industrial leasing activity, declining vacancy, and demand from advanced manufacturing and AI-driven companies. GRE plans energy-efficiency upgrades.
stories.impact: Minimal direct multifamily impact; however, advanced manufacturing and AI job concentration in Milpitas signals high-wage employment clustering that will drive regional demand for Class-B and Class-C multifamily in secondary Silicon Valley and East Bay submarkets. Developers should track AI-driven industrial infill areas as future residential demand sources.

stories.title: Fully Leased Meatpacking District Mixed-Use Refinanced for $293M
stories.excerpt: Walker & Dunlop said Friday it arranged $293,200,000 to refinance 40 Tenth Ave., a 158,957-square-foot, mixed-use property in Manhattan’s Meatpacking District. Walker & Dunlop Capital Markets Institutional Advisory advised Aurora Capital and William Gottlieb Real Estate. Dustin Stolly, Aaron Appel, Jonathan Schwartz, Keith Kurland, Adam Schwartz, Sean Reimer, Jordan Casella and Stanley Cayre arranged the fixed-rate, permanent debt refinancing from Corebridge Financial, Inc. “40 Tenth Ave. stands out in building quality, location and experience, all elements that differentiate a property for tenants,” said Stolly. “The fully leased office component, institutional tenant roster and substantial outdoor space demonstrate the continued demand for high-touch, well-located workplaces in New York.” Completed in 2019 and designed by Studio Gang, 40 Tenth Ave. includes 112,241 square feet of office space across floors three through 10 and 46,716 square feet of retail on the ground and second floors. Hyundai Motor occupies the property’s entire retail component, while office tenants include Starwood Capital Group, WestCap Management, RTW Investments, Stripes and Checkout.com. The post Fully Leased Meatpacking District Mixed-Use Refinanced for $293M appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Walker & Dunlop arranges $293.2M refi of 40 Tenth Ave, Manhattan Meatpacking, fixed-rate permanent.
158,957 sf mixed-use (112k sf office, 47k sf retail); 100% leased to institutional tenants.
Corebridge Financial lender; fully leased office and premium location support refinancing demand.
stories.summary: Walker & Dunlop arranged a $293.2 million fixed-rate, permanent refinancing for 40 Tenth Avenue, a 158,957-sf mixed-use property in Manhattan's Meatpacking District completed in 2019. The property comprises 112,241 sf of office (floors 3–10) and 46,716 sf of retail (ground and second floors), fully leased to institutional tenants including Hyundai Motor (retail), Starwood Capital Group, WestCap Management, and others. Corebridge Financial provided the debt.
stories.impact: Minimal direct multifamily impact; office-focused transaction. However, sustained refinancing demand for fully leased Manhattan mixed-use properties at $1,845/sf total valuation signals institutional capital remains available for trophy assets in prime NYC locations—a proxy for capital market confidence in mixed-use development feasibility in similar markets.

stories.title: Asian-American Deli Café Hestia Signs 8K-SF Lease at 570 Lexington Avenue
stories.excerpt: A cafe serving Asian and American cuisine is opening a fourth Manhattan location, Commercial Observer has learned. Café Hestia, a group of family-run delis, has signed a 20-year, 8,000-square-foot lease at the base of the Feil Organization’s 570 Lexington Avenue, which it will likely also use as a catering facility, according to tenant broker Kassin Sabbagh Realty (KSR). KSR did not immediately disclose the asking rent, but the average asking rent for the nearby retail corridor along Fifth Avenue from East 42nd to East 49th streets was $575 per square foot in the second quarter of 2026, according to a report from CBRE. “Our strategy has remained focused on finding operators that create lasting value for our tenants and the surrounding neighborhood, and Café Hestia builds on that vision with its all-day dining concept and wide variety of offerings,” Jordan Goldblum, director of retail leasing at the Feil Organization, said in a statement. Goldblum and Randall Briskin negotiated on behalf of the landlord in-house, while KSR’s Albert Manopla and Jack Khaski handled the deal for Café Hestia. KSR did not immediately provide a comment. Café Hestia’s other Manhattan locations are at 686 Third Avenue by Grand Central Terminal, 513 Seventh Avenue near Pennsylvania Station, and 80 Maiden Lane in the Financial District. Other tenants in the 50-story landmarked skyscraper on Lexington Avenue, also known as the General Electric Building, include international litigation firm Wolf Popper, which signed a 13,400-square-foot lease in December 2025, as well as the Real Estate Board of New York, which has a 23,031-square-foot office. Mark Hallum can be reached at mhallum@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: Café Hestia signs 20-year, 8,000-sf lease at 570 Lexington Ave, Manhattan (fourth location).
Area asking rent averages $575/sf (Fifth Ave, E42–E49 corridor, Q2 2026).
Family-run operator expanding; flagship location in high-traffic office/retail corridor.
stories.summary: Café Hestia, a family-run Asian-American deli-café group, signed a 20-year, 8,000-sf lease at the base of 570 Lexington Avenue (Feil Organization) for its fourth Manhattan location, with plans to use space for dining and catering. The retail corridor along Fifth Avenue from East 42nd to East 49th streets averaged $575/sf asking rent in Q2 2026.
stories.impact: Minimal direct multifamily impact; retail operator expansion. However, sustained high street-level retail asking rents ($575/sf) in Midtown East signal strong foot traffic and underlying office/residential density—a supportive factor for mixed-use infill development in Midtown submarkets but does not directly indicate multifamily demand signals.

stories.title: Edgewood Capital Provides $28M Refi for Fort Lauderdale Condo Project
stories.excerpt: Latitude Group has landed a $27.9 million loan to refinance a newly completed condominium project in Fort Lauderdale, Fla., Commercial Observer has learned. Edgewood Capital supplied the loan for the Terraces condo tower set to debut this fall, sources familiar with the deal told CO. Latitude Group previously secured a $24.5 million construction loan from Linkvest Capital in June 2024 to build the 22-unit development at 527 Orton Avenue, The Real Deal reported at the time. BayBridge Real Estate Capital arranged the refi with a team consisting of AJ Felberbaum, Jay Miller, Spencer Miller and Noah Rothman. Latitude acquired the half-ace development site for the project in 2020 for $3.3 million, according to TRD, citing property records. Sixty percent of the condos at the Terraces have been sold, according to the property’s website. The property’s amenities include a fitness center, a yoga studio, a swimming pool, cabanas and a community kitchen. Edgewood Capital, Latitude Group and BayBridge Real Estate Capital did not immediately return requests for comment. Andrew Coen can be reached at acoen@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: Edgewood Capital provides $27.9M refi for Terraces condo tower, Fort Lauderdale Beach, 22 units.
60% pre-sold; construction loan from Linkvest Capital (June 2024, $24.5M); site acquired 2020, $3.3M.
Luxury condo tower with full amenity suite; fall 2025 delivery.
stories.summary: Latitude Group secured a $27.9 million refinancing loan from Edgewood Capital for the Terraces, a newly completed 22-unit luxury condominium tower at 527 Orton Avenue in Fort Lauderdale Beach. The project, which received a $24.5 million construction loan from Linkvest Capital in June 2024, has pre-sold 60% of units as of delivery (fall 2025). The developer acquired the half-acre site in 2020 for $3.3 million.
stories.impact: Minimal direct multifamily developer impact; condo-for-sale product. However, 60% pre-sales on a 22-unit luxury tower in Fort Lauderdale Beach signals strong investor/owner-occupant demand in premium South Florida coastal submarkets—a positive sign for multifamily rents and future acquisition valuations in Fort Lauderdale proper, though condo projects do not compete directly with rental apartments.

stories.title: Decron Properties Buys 163-Unit Property in L.A.’s Miracle Mile for $114M
stories.excerpt: Decron Properties has acquired a 163-unit property in Los Angeles’ Miracle Mile for $114 million as the firm’s first L.A. deal in nearly two years. The Los Angeles-based investment firm acquired the asset at 5550 Wilshire Boulevard, a residential and retail property developed in 2010, at what Decron described as a substantial discount to replacement cost. After focusing on Sun Belt markets, the firm said it continues to pursue opportunities across Los Angeles, San Jose, Orange County, San Diego and Seattle as well. “Our growth-market strategy has never been a referendum on Los Angeles,” Decron President and CEO David Nagel said in a statement. “For a period, the risk-adjusted returns here simply weren’t competitive with what we were finding in the Sun Belt markets.” Nagel added that Los Angeles remains “one of the nation’s most important and chronically undersupplied housing markets,” where new supply is difficult and expensive to build. 5550 Wilshire includes one-, two- and three-bedroom apartments and townhomes. Amenities include a pool and spa, a resident lounge, a private movie theater and rooftop lounges. The property also includes 14,686 square feet of ground-floor retail that is fully leased to tenants that include Chipotle, Five Guys and FedEx Office. JLL’s Blake Rogers represented both Decron and the seller in the transaction. Decron owns and manages nearly 10,000 multifamily units and about 1 million square feet of retail across California, Washington and Arizona, with a portfolio totaling roughly 8.7 million square feet. Gregory Cornfield can be reached at gcornfield@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: Decron Properties acquires 5550 Wilshire Boulevard, L.A. Miracle Mile, 163-unit apt, $114M.
First L.A. deal in ~2 years; purchased at substantial discount to replacement cost.
Post-Sun Belt focus, firm resuming L.A. investment citing chronic undersupply and difficult new construction.
stories.summary: Decron Properties acquired 5550 Wilshire Boulevard, a 163-unit apartment property in Los Angeles' Miracle Mile, for $114 million—the firm's first LA deal in nearly two years. The 2010-built residential/retail asset was purchased at a substantial discount to replacement cost. Decron, which had focused on Sun Belt markets, is resuming LA investment, citing the region as a chronically undersupplied housing market where new construction is difficult and expensive.
stories.impact: Strong signal that institutional multifamily investors view Los Angeles as re-entry-worthy after a two-year hiatus—replacement-cost discount suggests cap rates have risen enough to justify acquisitions over new development. For Decron's statement on chronic undersupply and construction friction, expect continued competition for stabilized LA assets and potential for rent growth if deliveries remain constrained; developers should accelerate entitlements in LA submarkets (Westside, Central LA) to compete for institutional capital returning to the market.

stories.title: Corebridge Financial Refis Meatpacking Office Property With $293M Loan
stories.excerpt: A joint venture between Aurora Capital Associates and William Gottlieb Real Estate has sealed a $293 million loan to refinance a mixed-use asset in Manhattan’s Meatpacking District, according to a release. Corebridge Financial provided the fixed-rate, permanent loan on the 158,957-square-foot building at 40 10th Avenue. The 2019-built property features 112,241 square feet of office space and 46,176 square feet of retail on the first two floors. Walker & Dunlop negotiated the debt with a team consisting of Dustin Stolly, Aaron Appel, Jonathan Schwartz, Keith Kurland, Adam Schwartz, Sean Reimer, Jordan Casella and Stanley Cayre. “40 10th Avenue stands out in building quality, location and experience — all elements that differentiate a property for tenants,” Stolly, senior managing director of the capital markets institutional advisory team at Walker & Dunlop, said in a statement. “The fully leased office component, institutional tenant roster and substantial outdoor space demonstrate the continued demand for high-touch, well-located workplaces in New York.” The 10-story building has office tenants that include Starwood Capital Group, WestCap Management, RTW Investments, Stripes and Checkout.com. The retail portion of the property is occupied by Hyundai Motor. The property is positioned for success, according to Walker & Dunlop, since the Meatpacking District is one of Manhattan’s most supply-constrained office and retail submarkets. Aurora Capital Associates and William Gottlieb Real Estate landed a $150 million loan from Deutsche Pfandbriefbank in June 2020 to refinance construction debt to build the property, CO first reported at the time. Corebridge Financial, Aurora Capital and William Gottlieb Real Estate did not immediately return requests for comment. Andrew Coen can be reached at acoen@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: Corebridge Financial refis 40 Tenth Ave, Manhattan Meatpacking mixed-use, $293M fixed-rate permanent loan.
158,957 sf; 112,241 sf office (fully leased), 46,176 sf retail; 2019-built (Studio Gang).
Institutional office/retail tenants; deal underscores demand for high-quality, well-located workplaces.
stories.summary: Aurora Capital and William Gottlieb Real Estate closed a $293 million fixed-rate, permanent refinancing on 40 10th Avenue, a 158,957-sf mixed-use property in Manhattan's Meatpacking District. The 2019-built asset comprises 112,241 sf of office space (floors 3–10) and 46,176 sf of retail on the ground and second floors, fully leased to institutional tenants. Corebridge Financial provided the debt; Walker & Dunlop negotiated.
stories.impact: Duplicate/near-identical to Article 5; minimal direct multifamily impact. Validates that trophy office-retail assets in prime Manhattan locations retain refinancing capacity and institutional lender interest—a signal of overall NYC CRE market stability, but does not indicate multifamily-specific demand or supply shifts.

stories.title: Stroller Brand Uppababy Relocates Store to 156 Montague Street in Brooklyn Heights
stories.excerpt: Known for its distinctive strollers, baby gear brand Uppababy is relocating its store within Brooklyn, Commercial Observer has learned. The high-end baby accessories brand is opening a 3,780-square-foot brick-and-mortar location at Owen Realty’s 156 Montague Street in Brooklyn Heights, according to broker JLL. Uppababy will move next year from 90 Smith Street in Cobble Hill, where it established its Brooklyn retail and service “hub” in about 2019. JLL did not immediately provide the length of the lease or the asking rent for the space, but the average retail asking rent along nearby Fulton Street was $190 per square foot in 2025, according to the most recent retail report from the Real Estate Board of New York. “Brooklyn is an important market for Uppababy, and this relocation allows us to build on the relationships we have developed with local families,” Bob Monahan, co-founder and CEO of Uppababy, said in a statement. “Brooklyn Heights has a strong community of young and growing families, and the Montague Street location gives us the space and accessibility to deliver the hands-on product experience and personalized service that define our hub stores.” Uppababy manufactures and sells strollers, car seats, highchairs and other products for infants. Its top-of-the-line Vista V3 stroller, described on the company’s website as a “best seller,” retails for $1,000. JLL’s Jesse Wolff and Elijah Mehl represented the tenant in the transaction while Ryan Condren and George Danut, also from JLL, negotiated on behalf of Owen Realty. Owen Realty, which uses the LLC Montague Realty Development Associates, did not immediately respond to a request for comment. “Montague Street offers the neighborhood density, visibility and accessibility that work well for family focused retailers like Uppababy,” Wolff said in a statement. Mark Hallum can be reached at mhallum@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: Uppababy relocates retail location to 156 Montague Street, Brooklyn Heights, 3,780 sf; moves from Cobble Hill.
Nearby Fulton Street retail average asking rent $190/sf (2025); strong family demographic.
Premium baby brand expansion signals sustained affluent family demand in Brooklyn.
stories.summary: Uppababy, a high-end baby accessories brand, is relocating its Brooklyn store to 156 Montague Street in Brooklyn Heights (Owen Realty) in 2026, moving from its 90 Smith Street location in Cobble Hill established ~2019. The new 3,780-sf space will serve as retail and service hub. Nearby Fulton Street retail averaged $190/sf asking rent in 2025.
stories.impact: Retail tenant move itself has minimal direct impact; however, Uppababy's relocation to Brooklyn Heights (from Cobble Hill) signals continued strength of young families and affluent demographics in gentrified Brooklyn neighborhoods. This supports multifamily developer interest in Class-A rental development in Brooklyn Heights, Carroll Gardens, and nearby brownstone belt submarkets targeting young families—validating rent and absorption assumptions for family-oriented product in the borough.
